other.label: CBO cost estimate: S. 1441, Service Dogs Assisting Veterans Act of 2025

summary: The SAVES Act of 2025 requires the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) to set up a five-year pilot program to award competitive grants to nonprofit groups. These nonprofits will use the funds to provide specially trained service dogs to eligible veterans who have conditions such as visual impairments, hearing loss, mobility issues, post-traumatic stress disorder, or traumatic brain injuries. The VA must also provide commercial veterinary insurance policies for the dogs given to veterans through this program.

affected_groups.effect: Veterans with specified conditions, such as PTSD, traumatic brain injuries, visual or hearing impairments, and mobility issues, can receive service dogs free of charge and obtain ongoing veterinary insurance coverage for the dogs.
Eligible nonprofits can apply for competitive grants of up to $2 million per fiscal year from the VA to develop, implement, and manage programs providing service dogs to veterans.

key_provisions: Requires the VA to establish a five-year pilot program awarding competitive grants to nonprofit entities to provide service dogs to eligible veterans.
Sets a maximum grant amount of $2 million per fiscal year for each nonprofit entity, subject to potential increases under certain conditions.
Authorizes appropriations of $10 million for each of the five consecutive fiscal years of the pilot program.
Requires the VA to provide a commercially available veterinary insurance policy for every service dog provided through the grant program, continuing even after the pilot ends.
Prohibits grant-receiving nonprofit entities from charging any fees to veterans receiving service dogs through the program.
Defines eligible veterans to include those with specific conditions such as blindness, loss of limbs, hearing loss, PTSD, traumatic brain injury, or other conditions approved by the VA.
missing_information: The total overall federal budget impact beyond the authorized $10 million per year is not fully detailed outside of the specific fiscal year authorizations.
The exact number of veterans who will ultimately receive service dogs through the pilot program is not specified.
summary_detail.plain_summary: The SAVES Act of 2025 requires the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) to set up a five-year pilot program to award competitive grants to nonprofit groups. These nonprofits will use the funds to provide specially trained service dogs to eligible veterans who have conditions such as visual impairments, hearing loss, mobility issues, post-traumatic stress disorder, or traumatic brain injuries. The VA must also provide commercial veterinary insurance policies for the dogs given to veterans through this program.
summary_detail.significance: The bill creates a federal grant program and funding stream within the Department of Veterans Affairs dedicated to expanding the availability of service dogs for veterans with specific physical and psychological conditions.
